title: Problem Solving
tagline: Turn unfamiliar problems into clear models, reliable solutions, and better decisions
summary: A deep, language-independent textbook on the reasoning process behind solving problems in software and beyond: clarifying requirements, modeling state, decomposing complexity, designing algorithms, proving correctness, testing adversarial cases, debugging, evaluating trade-offs, communicating solutions, and learning systematically from failure. It distinguishes problem solving from syntax memorization and connects the method to data structures, architecture, APIs, databases, and production engineering.
topics: Problem statements, requirements, and success criteria
Greedy choices, recursion, and dynamic programming
Working with unfamiliar systems and documentation
Learning from mistakes and building reusable intuition
